blocks.content: Sound is a form of mechanical energy that produces the sensation of hearing. It is produced due to vibrations of objects and travels through a medium in the form of sound waves. Sound is essential for communication, music and many scientific applications.
1. Meaning of Sound

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Sound is a form of energy produced by vibrating objects and travels as longitudinal mechanical waves.
Sound requires a material medium (solid, liquid, or gas) for propagation and cannot travel through a vacuum.
The loudness of sound depends on its amplitude, while the pitch or shrillness depends on its frequency.
An echo is formed by the reflection of sound waves from a distant obstacle, requiring a minimum distance of 17.2 metres.
Ultrasound refers to sound frequencies greater than 20,000 Hz and is widely used in medical imaging, cleaning, and SONAR.

blocks.content: • Sound is a form of energy that produces the sensation of hearing.
• It is produced by vibrating objects.
• Sound travels through a medium in the form of waves.
• It cannot travel through vacuum because it requires a material medium.
2. Production of Sound
• Sound is produced when an object vibrates.
• The vibrating object causes nearby particles of the medium to vibrate.
• These vibrations travel through the medium as sound waves.
3. Sound Waves
Sound waves are longitudinal waves consisting of compressions and rarefactions.
• Compression – region of high pressure.
• Rarefaction – region of low pressure.
4. Characteristics of Sound Waves
Sound waves are longitudinal mechanical waves that require a material medium for propagation and cannot travel through a vacuum.
5. Types of Sound
6. Speed of Sound
The speed of sound depends on the medium and temperature. It travels fastest in solids and slowest in gases.
7. Reflection of Sound
When sound waves strike a surface, they bounce back. This phenomenon is called reflection of sound.

rows: Human voice, musical instruments, everyday noises

blocks.content: 8. Echo
• Echo is the repetition of sound caused by reflection of sound waves.
• It is heard when sound reflects from a distant surface.
• The minimum distance required to hear echo is about 17 meters.
9. Uses of Ultrasound
• Medical imaging (ultrasound scanning)
• Detecting cracks in metals
• SONAR used by ships to detect underwater objects
• Cleaning delicate electronic components
10. Noise Pollution
• Noise pollution refers to unwanted or harmful sound.

items: Speed of sound varies by state of matter: Maximum in solids, intermediate in liquids, and minimum in gases (V_solid > V_liquid > V_gas).
The minimum distance required between the source and obstacle to hear a distinct echo is 17.2 m at 20°C.
SONAR (Sound Navigation and Ranging) utilizes ultrasound waves to measure sea depth and locate underwater objects.
Frequency determines the pitch of sound; higher frequency results in a higher pitch.

blocks.content: • It can cause hearing problems and stress.
• Sources include traffic, industrial machines and loudspeakers.
Important Facts
• Sound cannot travel in vacuum.
• Human hearing range is 20 Hz to 20,000 Hz.
• Sound waves are longitudinal waves.
• Speed of sound in air is about 343 m/s.
